verdict: Constellation's net sales rose 6% as beer shipments grew and wine & spirits bounced back 17%, but a $50M asset impairment and heavier brand spending cut operating income 8% — reported EPS still rose 25% because the tax bill was roughly half last year's.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: net sales of $2,633M vs $2,481M a year ago

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: first half of FY27, up 4% vs a year ago

segments.name: Beer
segments.note: Modelo, Corona, Pacifico and the other imported beers — net sales rose 5% on a 5.5% increase in shipment volumes, and the business was the #1 dollar share gainer in U.S. beer.

segments.name: Wine and Spirits
segments.note: Kim Crawford, The Prisoner, Mi CAMPO tequila and other brands — net sales jumped 17% on a 15.4% rise in shipments, swinging the segment back to a small operating profit.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs — up from $436M a year ago on increased marketing investment and other spending behind the brands.

opex.name: Asset impairment
opex.note: Impairment and related expenses — mainly writing down assets held for sale tied to the planned divestiture of the Nelson's Green Brier business.

otherDetail: Below operating income: $8M of income from unconsolidated investments, minus $83M of net interest expense, gives net other expense of $76M (actual -$75.6M before rounding).
footerNote: Net income was $582M; after the $16M share belonging to noncontrolling interests (actual $16.5M), net income attributable to Constellation (CBI) was $566M. Figures are rounded to the nearest $M, so the attribution line is shown as $16M to balance exactly.

takeaways.title: Beer still carries the company
takeaways.text: Beer was $2,474M of the $2,633M total — 94% of net sales — and grew 5% on higher shipments, even though depletions (what drinkers actually took off shelves) slipped 0.6% as Modelo Especial and Corona Extra softened.

takeaways.title: An impairment ate the growth
takeaways.text: A $49.8M asset impairment, mainly on assets held for sale for the planned Nelson's Green Brier divestiture, plus much higher SG&A, pushed operating income down 8% to $805M despite the sales growth. On the company's 'comparable' basis operating income was $897M.

takeaways.title: A lighter tax bill lifted EPS
takeaways.text: The tax provision fell to $147M from $297M a year ago, so net income attributable to Constellation rose 21% to $566M and EPS rose 25% to $3.32, even though operating income fell.

oneTimers: $49.8M of asset impairment and related expenses, mainly impairments on assets held for sale for the planned Nelson's Green Brier divestiture and the New Zealand wine divestitures.

Total 'comparable adjustments' cut GAAP operating income by $91.6M in the quarter ($71.5M after tax, $0.42 per share) — including the impairment, strategic reconfiguration and restructuring costs, and commodity-derivative settlements; comparable EPS was $3.74 vs reported $3.32.
